Arabic mainly uses ⁧إِلَّا⁩ , with rules of chance changing according to the phrase, and then ⁧غَيْر⁩ , ⁧سِوَى⁩ , ⁧مَا عَدَا⁩ and ⁧بِاسْتِثْنَاءِ⁩ . Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. use ⁧إِلَّا⁩ in a complete affirmative sentence, with the exception of the accusative;
2. use the restriction ⁧لَا⁩ / ⁧مَا⁩ / ⁧لَمْ⁩ / ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ … ⁧إِلَّا⁩ • only, only in the case required by the sentence;
3. use ⁧غَيْر⁩ and ⁧سِوَى⁩ with the genitive;
4. recognize and use ⁧مَا عَدَا⁩ and ⁧بِاسْتِثْنَاءِ⁩ in formal texts;
5. distinguish ⁧فَقَط⁩ , ⁧لَا⁩ … ⁧إِلَّا⁩ and ⁧إِنَّمَا⁩ ;
6. translate the exception and restriction with the most natural Italian forms.

In Italian  "solo" is an adverb; in Arabic ⁧لَا⁩ … ⁧إِلَّا⁩ is often more natural than ⁧فَقَط⁩ , especially in the text: ⁧لَا يُسْمَحُ بِالدُّخُولِ إِلَّا لِلْمُوَظَّفِينَ⁩ The entry is permitted only to the staff.
